IDXX.thesis_one_line: Near-duopoly veterinary diagnostics compounder with recurring reagent revenue, but priced for the same growth it needs to deliver — no margin of safety.
kill_criteria: CAG Diagnostics organic recurring-revenue growth < 5% for two consecutive quarters
A guidance cut (vs. the immediately preceding range) on revenue or comparable EPS
GAAP-vs-comparable EPS gap widens beyond the current ~10-15% spread without a disclosed one-time driver
U.S. clinical-visit growth (management's own disclosed metric) turns negative by more than 2% for two consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: U.S. companion-animal clinical visits have been flat-to-down for several years; management calls this a persistent headwind every quarter
Paid an ~$80 million judgment in April 2025 to conclude a legacy 2004-2017 patent-royalty dispute
Revenue growth decelerated from +14.3% YoY (Q1 2026) to +9.7% YoY (Q2 2026), partly on a disclosed $15M FX headwind
Insider-selling summary relied on a secondary aggregator (simplywall.st), not primary Form 4s
data_conflicts: d4 vendor trailing FCF-yield field (2.2%) implies TTM FCF ~$909M, materially below this dossier's SEC-filing-derived TTM FCF (~$1,254M); likely a different trailing-window/capex definition in the vendor feed, not reconciled further
IDXX.confidence_in_thesis: medium: quality and moat are well evidenced from primary filings; the valuation reconciliation (implied ~ base) is a close judgment call with limited margin of safety

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for IDXX (outside the original 69-name V1 universe). Own reverse DCF: implied 10-yr FCF growth ~9.4% (EV $41.34B, TTM FCF $1.254B, WACC 8.5%, terminal 3.5%) vs. an independent base-case estimate of ~9-10%/yr organic-plus-buyback growth — implied_vs_base = in_line.

IDXX.scenario_basis: Starting TTM GAAP EPS $14.23 (Q3'25-Q2'26); base: EPS growth ~11%/yr decelerating from FY26 guided 13-15% comparable growth, NTM P/E compresses 32x->28x (-4.3%/yr), no dividend; bear: EPS growth ~5%/yr on persistent US visit weakness, multiple compresses to peer-level 22x (-11.9%/yr); bull: EPS growth ~16%/yr on new-instrument reacceleration, multiple holds ~32x.

ISRG.thesis_one_line: Global leader in robotic surgery with a large recurring-instrument installed base, but real antitrust-appeal risk and a rich multiple leave little room for error.
kill_criteria: Worldwide da Vinci procedure growth < 10% YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs. guided 13.5-15.5% for FY2026)
An adverse or unfavorable-settlement outcome in the Restore Robotics 11th Circuit appeal that opens the EndoWrist repair/service market to third parties
Full-year non-GAAP gross-margin guidance cut below the current 67-68% range
Two consecutive quarters of da Vinci system placement growth (units) turning negative YoY
A debt-funded acquisition or buyback program that takes the company's net-cash position negative
key_adverse_facts: A federal judge found evidence a jury could conclude Intuitive engaged in tying/exclusive dealing to maintain monopoly power over EndoWrist instrument repair (Rebotix Repair case, settled 2025); a related case (Restore Robotics) was on appeal at the 11th Circuit as of December 2025
Stock declined roughly 30% during 2026 per third-party coverage, attributed to the Medtronic Hugo competitive launch and procedure-growth deceleration concerns
Management itself guided a sharp deceleration in da Vinci procedure growth, from 18% realized in 2025 to 13-15% guided for 2026, later narrowed to 13.5-15.5%
Large GAAP-vs-adjusted earnings gap driven by SBC (~7-8% of revenue): TTM GAAP P/E ~46.5x vs NTM (adjusted) P/E ~34.5x
data_conflicts: d4 vendor 'totalCash' field ($5.2B) is materially higher than the strict XBRL CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue at 2026-06-30 ($2.76B); the difference is attributable to short-term marketable-securities investments included in the vendor aggregate but not the strict cash line
ISRG.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low: business quality and recurring-revenue moat are well evidenced, but the antitrust-appeal outcome and competitive response to Medtronic Hugo are genuine unresolved uncertainties this dossier could not close out within the time-box

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for ISRG. Own reverse DCF: implied 10-yr FCF growth ~12.6% (EV $136.05B, TTM FCF $3.223B, WACC 8.5%, terminal 3.5%) vs. an independent base-case estimate of ~11-13%/yr (guided 13.5-15.5% 2026 procedure growth, decelerating further over 10 years) - implied_vs_base = in_line, but this is a thin reconciliation with little cushion, hence 'full' rather than 'fair' on the dossier's own qualitative read.

ISRG.scenario_basis: Starting TTM GAAP EPS $8.72 (Q3'25-Q2'26); base: adjusted EPS growth ~14%/yr matching guided procedure growth, NTM (adjusted) P/E compresses 34.5x->30x (-4.6%/yr); bear: competitive share loss to Medtronic Hugo/J&J Ottava plus soft China capex slows growth to ~8%/yr, multiple compresses to peer-level 24x (-11.2%/yr); bull: da Vinci 5 and Ion upgrade cycles reaccelerate growth to ~17%/yr, multiple holds ~35x.

LIN.thesis_one_line: Largest global industrial-gas oligopoly with a record contracted backlog, but the price implies more growth than management's own guidance promises.
LIN.horizon: not held at current price; revisit if the multiple de-rates or backlog conversion accelerates growth above the guided 8-9% range
kill_criteria: Net debt/EBITDA > 2.25x (vs. 1.67x today) without a disclosed, value-accretive reason
Full-year adjusted-EPS guidance cut vs. the immediately preceding range
Project backlog shrinks (vs. the current $11B) for two consecutive quarterly disclosures
Underlying/organic sales growth < 2% for two consecutive quarters
GAAP net income growth negative for two consecutive quarters beyond what is explained by disclosed purchase-accounting/restructuring items
key_adverse_facts: Reverse DCF implies ~12.3% 10-yr FCF growth, well above management's own guided FY2026 adjusted-EPS growth of 8-9% and its stated long-term high-single-to-low-double-digit algorithm
Capex guidance raised twice in 2026 (from $5.0-5.5B to $5.5-6.0B) to fund the backlog, and TTM FCF/NI conversion has fallen to ~69% (from 74% in FY2025) as capex intensity rises
Q4 2025 GAAP net income fell 11% YoY (to $1,530M) on Linde AG merger purchase-accounting amortization and restructuring charges, versus adjusted net income up 4%
Net debt/EBITDA ~1.67x while leaning harder on the balance sheet for growth capex
data_conflicts: The Q1 2026 earnings-release exhibit could not be located/opened at its expected SEC accession path in this session; Q1 2026 guidance figures are corroborated via secondary coverage only, not independently re-opened from the primary document (disclosed as a data gap, not asserted as filing-verified)
LIN.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high: the guidance track record and backlog figures are directly filing-sourced and consistent; the valuation gap (implied vs. guided growth) is the clearest, best-evidenced finding in this batch

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for LIN. Own reverse DCF: implied 10-yr FCF growth ~12.3% (EV $240.47B, TTM FCF $4.975B, WACC 7.5%, terminal 3%) vs. an independent base-case estimate of ~8-10%/yr (management's own guided FY2026 adjusted-EPS growth of 8-9% and stated long-term algorithm) - implied_vs_base = above.

LIN.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 guided adjusted EPS midpoint $17.80; base: adjusted EPS growth ~9%/yr (management's own guided algorithm), NTM P/E compresses 26x->23x (-4.0%/yr), plus ~1.4% dividend yield; bear: industrial-production slowdown and backlog delays cut growth to ~3%/yr, multiple compresses to 19x (-10.0%/yr), plus dividend; bull: AI/electronics-driven backlog conversion accelerates growth to ~12%/yr, multiple holds ~26x, plus dividend.
